# `jS()` {#fn-js}

A05 checked the local June solar limit against annual obliquity and the specified parallax correction. [A05 results](a05-solar-limits.qmd).

[Function index](function-index.html#idx-js)

```{=html}
<p>The June solstice is represented by the positive obliquity of the ecliptic for the
requested epoch. The result is geocentric when no site is supplied. With a site, the
function subtracts the approximate parallax correction using latitude and target
altitude. This obliquity-based target does not determine a solstice time or a sunrise or
sunset bearing.
</p>
```

[Seasonal reference declinations](fn-ds.qmd).


<details><summary>Implementation arguments, return value and documented modes</summary>

```{=html}
<table><thead><tr><th>Argument</th><th>Formal default</th><th>Behaviour in this interface</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row"><code>year</code></th><td><code>skyscapeR.env$cur.year</code></td><td><p>Astronomical year. The default is the current year in the package settings. Historical labels such as <code>"3700 BC"</code> are accepted by <code>astroYear</code>.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>loc</code></th><td><code>FALSE</code></td><td><p>Latitude in degrees north or a <code>skyscapeR.horizon</code> object. Omit this argument or use <code>FALSE</code> for geocentric declination.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>parallax</code></th><td><code>0.00224</code></td><td><p>Mean horizontal parallax in degrees. The default is 0.00224 degrees for the Sun.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>altitude</code></th><td><code>0</code></td><td><p>Altitude of the sun. Defaults to 0 degrees.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>verbose</code></th><td><code>TRUE</code></td><td><p>Logical to control output of warnings and messages.
Defaults to TRUE.</p></td></tr></tbody></table><h5>Return value</h5><p>Numeric declination in degrees. With loc = FALSE the result is geocentric. Supplying a location applies the parallax correction for the chosen altitude.
</p>
```

</details>
